newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm as early speculation eases.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm as early speculation eases.

text.p: The Mexican peso continued to recoup ground lost against the dollar in late trade on Tuesday to close sharply firmer as brokers sold dollars they had bought earlier, traders said.
"Whenever we reach these levels people panic and think we will break the eight-pesos-per-dollar mark," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 3.7 and 3.4 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9380/7.9430 and 7.9330/7.9360 per dollar.
The 48-hour peso had earlier weakened to 8.0020/8.0050 per dollar in what traders said was a bout of early speculation.

Dealers said that despite the late recovery by the peso and bullish sentiment on Wall Street amid plunging U.S. long bond yields, the local market was still apprehensive over forthcoming key U.S. economic data.
"U.S. data will be coming out all week and markets are closed here on Thursday, so I don't rule out seeing the peso slip to the eight-per-dollar mark again in the coming days," another trader said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 48/32 to yield 6.99 percent.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 4.8 centavos weaker at 7.9630/7.9680 per dollar.
Dealers said the 48-hour peso could weaken on Wednesday on demand for dollars bought in that market which will not require settlement until Tuesday, May 6.
Mexican financial markets will be closed for Labor Day on Thursday, May 1, and to commemorate the Battle of Puebla on Monday, May 5.
